description:
I'm an AI agent builder from Pune with an MBA in Finance, working across AI agents, autonomous systems, and Web3.

One of my favorite projects was Hermes Mars Rover, where I used Nous Research's Hermes AI agent with a Curiosity rover simulation. It earned 5th place among 188 participants in a Nous Research hackathon.

I'm now building MarsShield independently, bringing my interest in Mars exploration, AI, and scientific research together through real NASA rover data and interactive technology.
summary:
MarsShield is an interactive Martian radiation research platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It combines real NASA rover measurements, planetary terrain data, atmospheric observations, and published radiation transport simulations to investigate cosmic radiation across three regions of Mars: Gale Crater, Jezero Crater, and Olympus Mons.

At Gale Crater, MarsShield analyzes radiation measurements from NASA's Curiosity rover, tests terrain shielding models, and provides an interactive Marswalk planning experience. At Jezero and Olympus Mons, it calculates exploratory radiation estimates using published simulations and atmospheric models.

Users can explore authentic 3D Martian terrain, compare radiation exposure under different conditions, investigate scientific evidence, and download reproducible research datasets.

MarsShield makes complex planetary science accessible while clearly distinguishing actual measurements from model predictions. It supports education, planetary research, and the exploration of future human missions to Mars.
details:
The Challenge

Mars has a thin atmosphere and lacks a global magnetic field, exposing its surface to galactic cosmic radiation. Understanding how radiation varies with atmospheric conditions and terrain is important for future exploration. However, direct surface radiation measurements are geographically limited.

Our Solution

MarsShield combines measured radiation evidence, atmospheric science, radiation transport simulations, and interactive 3D terrain exploration in one publicly accessible research platform.

Three Research Regions

Gale Crater: We analyze NASA Curiosity RAD measurements at 322 rover stops, together with REMS atmospheric pressure observations and detailed orbital terrain data. Users can test radiation shielding models against observations, investigate uncertainty, and plan hypothetical science Marswalks with different routes and activity durations.

Jezero Crater: We use published radiation transport models and atmospheric pressure information, checked against Perseverance MEDA observations, to estimate cosmic radiation exposure. Users can explore authentic terrain, the rover traverse, and location dependent atmospheric conditions.

Olympus Mons: We model cosmic radiation exposure in the volcano's caldera using published simulations and Mars Climate Database atmospheric conditions. Users can investigate high altitude Martian terrain and compare modeled exposure with the other regions.

Scientific Methods and Findings

MarsShield reproduces published radiation calculations and tests terrain shielding models against NASA observations. Across 322 Curiosity stops, incorporating terrain reduced the held out prediction error by 11.7% relative to a time only baseline. This improvement is concentrated in strongly sheltered locations and is not proof of accurate dose predictions at new sites.

Our regional model estimates annual effective dose rates of 168.9 mSv at Gale, 167.8 mSv at Jezero, and 161.8 mSv at Olympus Mons under a common 700 MV solar modulation scenario. These are exploratory model estimates, not measured exposure rates or astronaut safety assessments.

Technology and Innovation

MarsShield uses Python for scientific processing and validation; TypeScript, React, Next.js, and Three.js for interactive exploration; and published AtRIS/Geant4 simulations for regional radiation calculations.

The platform integrates orbital terrain, rover observations, atmospheric modeling, interactive charts, radiation comparisons, mission planning, and reproducible CSV and research package exports.

Its innovation lies in connecting real planetary measurements with transparent scientific models and making the results explorable in a public web application.

Impact

MarsShield can help students, educators, and researchers explore how radiation exposure on Mars depends on atmospheric conditions and surrounding terrain. It also provides an experimental foundation for future mission planning research.

Scientific Transparency

Direct radiation measurements are available at Gale, while Jezero and Olympus Mons use exploratory estimates. Terrain shielding outside Gale, solar storm predictions, spacesuit protection, and astronaut health risks are not modeled. MarsShield explicitly distinguishes measured results, model predictions, and assumptions.
